title: One park plan, two solvers

blocks.text: A city's parks department (not GridCap) picks improvements for one park within a budget. Some improvements need another one (`requires`: `(a, b)`, a needs b) and some pairs exclude each other (`excludes`: `(a, b)`). The department's analyst wants the model in both CP-SAT and MathOpt, to check one against the other before choosing a solver.
Write two functions in `twins.py`, each returning the best total value as an `int`:

items: `best_with_cpsat(value, cost, budget, requires, excludes)`: the model in CP-SAT, with the two rules written as logic constraints;
`best_with_highs(value, cost, budget, requires, excludes)`: the same model in MathOpt, with the rules as linear rows, solved with HiGHS.

blocks.text: The model, with $`I`$ the improvements and $`x_i \in \{0, 1\}`$ "improvement $`i`$ is built":
The tests compare each function with a brute-force search. About twenty lines in all.

cost = {"bench": 10, "trail": 35, "pond": 30, "kiosk": 25, "swing": 20}
requires = [("kiosk", "trail")]
excludes = [("pond", "swing")]

for budget in (50, 80):
    print(f"budget {budget}, rules on, CP-SAT:", best_with_cpsat(value, cost, budget, requires, excludes))
    print(f"budget {budget}, rules on, HiGHS:", best_with_highs(value, cost, budget, requires, excludes))
print("budget 80, no rules, CP-SAT:", best_with_cpsat(value, cost, 80, [], []))

origin.section: On a Plain Selection Both Prove the Same Optimum

concepts: on a plain selection model both solvers prove the same optimum, so the choice is about modeling style
